'''Peter A. Schwerdtfeger''' (born 1 September 1955) is a German theoretical chemist based in New Zealand. He holds a chair in theoretical chemistry at [[Massey University]] (Albany, Auckland), is director of Massey's Centre for Theoretical Chemistry and Physics, and is head of the New Zealand Institute for Advanced Study (NZIAS).<ref name="MasseyProf">{{Cite web |title=Distinguished Professor Peter Schwerdtfeger |url=https://www.massey.ac.nz/massey/expertise/profile.cfm?stref=166830 |website=Massey University |access-date=2025-09-26}}</ref><ref name="CTCPcv">{{Cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae – Peter Schwerdtfeger |url=https://ctcp.massey.ac.nz/index.php?group=schwerd&menu=schwerd&page=cv_peter |website=Centre for Theoretical Chemistry and Physics (Massey University) |access-date=2025-09-26}}</ref><ref name="NZIASHead">{{Cite web |title=Contact us |url=https://www.nzias.ac.nz/contactus.html |website=New Zealand Institute for Advanced Study |access-date=2025-09-26}}</ref> He was elected to the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] in 2012<ref>{{Cite web |title=International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science |url=https://iaqms.org/members/schwerdtfeger.php |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=iaqms.org}}</ref> and received New Zealand's [[Rutherford Medal (Royal Society of New Zealand)|Rutherford Medal]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CTCP News & Publicity (25 June 2012): IAQMS election |url=https://ctcp.massey.ac.nz/index.php?group=&menu=publicity&page=publicity |website=CTCP (Massey University) |access-date=2025-09-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 Rutherford Medal: Understanding the fundamentals |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/medals-and-awards/medals-and-awards-news/2014-rutherford-medal-understanding-the-fundamentals/ |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi |date=26 November 2014 |access-date=2025-09-26}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Schwerdtfeger gained a qualification as a chemical-technical assistant at the Chemisches Institut Dr. Flad, Stuttgart, in 1973, and a chemical engineering degree from Aalen University of Applied Sciences in 1976. He studied chemistry, physics and mathematics at the [[University of Stuttgart]], completing the ''Dr. rer. nat.'' (PhD) in theoretical chemistry in 1986. He received the ''Habilitation'' and ''venia legendi'' from the [[Philipps University of Marburg]] in 1995.<ref name="CTCPcv" />

==Career==
In 1987 he moved to New Zealand on a Feodor-Lynen fellowship of the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation to the University of Auckland.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-14 |title=Alexander von Humboldt-Stiftung |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/ |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=www.humboldt-foundation.de |language=de}}</ref> He held a research fellowship at the Research School of Chemistry, [[Australian National University]] (1989–1991), then returned to Auckland as lecturer (1991) and later personal chair (1999). In 2004 he was appointed to the chair in theoretical chemistry at [[Massey University]] (Albany) and founded the Centre for Theoretical Chemistry and Physics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Crassous |first=Jeanne |last2=Chardonnet |first2=Christian |last3=Saue |first3=Trond |last4=Schwerdtfeger |first4=Peter |date=2005 |title=Recent experimental and theoretical developments towards the observation of parity violation effects in molecules by spectroscopy |journal=Organic & Biomolecular Chemistry |volume=3 |issue=12 |pages=2218–2224 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/7734971 |access-date=2025-09-26 |quote=Peter Schwerdtfeger received his PhD from Stuttgart University in 1986… Feodor-Lynen Fellow in 1987 (Auckland)… research fellow at ANU… lectureship in 1991… ''venia legendi'' (Marburg) in 1995… personal chair in 1999… chair at Massey in 2004.}}</ref><ref name="CTCPcv" />

He has served as head of the NZIAS, and is listed as head of Institute on the NZIAS site.<ref name="NZIASHead" /> He was the Gunnar Källén Lecturer in Physics at [[Lund University]] in 2015 and previously undertook a Royal Society of Chemistry Australasian Lectureship tour in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CTCP Annual Report 2015 |url=https://ctcp.massey.ac.nz/data/CTCP2015reportweb.pdf |website=CTCP (Massey University) |page=5 |access-date=2025-09-26 |quote=P. Schwerdtfeger was the Gunnar Källén Lecturer of 2015 at the University of Lund, Department of Physics.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=CTCP Annual Performance Report 2007 |url=https://ctcp.massey.ac.nz/data/CTCP2007reportweb.pdf |website=CTCP (Massey University) |page=3 |access-date=2025-09-26 |quote=P. Schwerdtfeger was awarded the 2007 Australasian Lectureship.}}</ref>

From 2017 to 2018 he was associated with the Centre for Advanced Study (CAS) in Oslo through the project "Molecules in Extreme Environments," hosted by Trygve Helgaker.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CTCP Annual Report 2017 |url=https://ctcp.massey.ac.nz/data/CTCP2017reportweb.pdf |website=CTCP (Massey University) |page=3 |access-date=2025-09-26}}</ref>

Schwerdtfeger has authored hundreds of research papers in electronic-structure theory and heavy-element chemistry; his CV lists more than 380 publications.<ref name="CTCPcv" />

== Fellowships and awards ==
Schwerdtfeger has received multiple national and international awards:

*2001 James Cook Fellowship<ref name="JamesCook">[https://royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/funds-and-opportunities/james-cook-research-fellowship/james-cook-research-fellowships-recipients/list-of-recipients/ Royal Society of New Zealand James Cook Fellowship: List of Recipients]</ref>
*2010 Humboldt Research Prize by the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt Foundation]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scientist wins prestigious Humboldt Prize {{!}} Scoop News |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/ED1011/S00117/scientist-wins-prestigious-humboldt-prize.htm |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=www.scoop.co.nz}}</ref>
*2011 Fukui Medal<ref name="IAQMS">[https://www.iaqms.org/members/schwerdtfeger.php International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]</ref> 
*2012 Fellow of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]].<ref name="IAQMS"/>
*2014 [[Royal Society of New Zealand]]'s [[Rutherford Medal (Royal Society of New Zealand)|Rutherford Medal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/2014/11/26/royal-society-of-new-zealand-recognises-achievements-of-researchers/ |title=Royal Society of New Zealand recognises achievements of researchers |date=26 November 2014 |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=27 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141220080825/http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/2014/11/26/royal-society-of-new-zealand-recognises-achievements-of-researchers/ |archive-date=20 December 2014 }}</ref><ref>"[http://www.nzherald.co.nz//nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11365088 Explosive start for NZ's highest science honour recipient]". ''The New Zealand Herald''. 28 November 2014.</ref>
*2019 [[Dan Walls|Dan Walls Medal]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=NZIP Award Recipients – New Zealand Institute of Physics |url=https://nzip.org.nz/about-nzip/nzip-award-recipients/ |access-date=2023-03-16 |language=en-US}}</ref>
